cohort: The study included 128 multiple (triplets and quadruplets) and 260 singleton infants admitted to a reference maternity hospital over a 7-year period.
finding: Major neonatal outcomes were largely similar between multiples and singletons when paired by gestational age and birth weight, though NEC incidence was significantly higher in triplets and mortality was higher in singletons.
birth_weight: Mean 1470 ± 461g for multiples and 1495 ± 540g for singletons.
gest_age: Mean 31.3 ± 2.5 weeks for multiples and 31.5 ± 2.8 weeks for singletons.
